title: Sideways Layer Calling (Intra-Layer Coupling)
pattern: A service or manager object directly instantiates and invokes another manager object residing within the same architectural layer.
why_bad: It violates layer encapsulation and creates sideways dependencies that make use cases non-independent. Changes to the internal workflows of `BillingManager` directly ripple into and break `OrderManager`.
detection: Direct instantiation or reference to a sibling class/struct in the same layer inside a method body.
counterexample: Standard utility modules or shared stateless helpers that do not manage domain workflows or use cases.
source: Juval Löwy, *Righting Software* (2019), Chapter 3 ("Structure" - Calling Sideways).
